risks: Source can change during root integration; this report is a hashed snapshot, not proof of current clean HEAD or dependency acceptance.
Form submit click, published issue status or queued mapping result is not the verified accepted response event required for Task creation.
Published Forms and recipe event names differ; unverified alias may trigger before accepted durable response or never trigger.
Existing PersonalTaskStore.create returns mutable in-memory data and lacks origin dedupe/assignee/durable revision receipt. Reusing it directly as production authority would underdeliver.
Expected LSX-WP-004 patchFields contract does not itself guarantee a create-with-origin or assignment API; creation/source binding must be explicitly established with LSX-WP-037/native owner.
Current TaskLink cannot directly type a FormResponseRef; fake note links or copied response text would lose provenance/ACL. Request owner-supported typed source binding rather than casts.

Event bus rate limit is 10 events/minute for non-SchedulerTick events; it drops and resolves void, and handler failures are swallowed. Advancing a durable outbox cursor from emit success would lose submissions.
Unknown-action config passthrough is not native validation or execution; graph currently accepts only registered event and prompt/webhook executable paths.
ResponseID-only dedup merges distinct source forms. Dedup by eventID alone or workflow revision may duplicate the same origin across repeated accepted events/replay.
Task commit, source binding, event acknowledgement and notification delivery have crash boundaries; process-memory dedup cannot satisfy restart recovery or one intended notification.
Task IDs are source-store/owner scoped; current workspace inference or Base-local copies would leak personal tasks and violate canonical identity.

The allowed shared files do not include command RPC, renderer inspector, locales, task types or schemas. Dependency extensibility or reviewed scope expansion is mandatory; no silent feature reduction.
Native intended-assignee capability is absent in inspected core types. Dropping owner mapping or notifying every workspace member is not an acceptable fallback.
UI criteria are mandatory for this specified inspector change; isolated fixture UI, structural report validation and toast success cannot close the package.
